# go-plus (trendvidia/go#20): the go command keys the build cache on the
# compiler's content ID, for a release toolchain as on the development
# branch. Upstream keys a release on its version string, which let a
# rebuilt compiler of the same version, or stock Go of the same version,
# be served this toolchain's cache entries.

# A tool linked externally has no build ID to report: gc.go leaves
# objabi.buildID unset when MustLinkExternal holds for the platform the
# tool is built for. [mustlinkext] asks the same of this script's
# GOOS/GOARCH, which start as the test binary's own platform, and so as
# the platform these tools were built for and run on.
[mustlinkext] skip

# The compiler and linker report their build IDs, whatever their version.
# (That a release in particular does so is pinned by
# cmd/internal/objabi's TestVersionFlagBuildID, which does not depend on
# this tree's VERSION.)
go tool compile -V=full
stdout '^compile version .* buildID=[^ /]+/[^ ]+$'
go tool link -V=full
stdout '^link version .* buildID=[^ /]+/[^ ]+$'

go build ./cmd/toolid
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache

# The baseline: the compiler as it is.
env TOOLID_REWRITE=none
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
cp stdout base.txt

# A compiler whose content differs must not be served the cached object.
env TOOLID_REWRITE=content
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
! cmp stdout base.txt

# Only the content counts: the action ID part of the compiler's own
# build ID does not change the key, as on the development branch.
env TOOLID_REWRITE=action
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
cmp stdout base.txt

# A tool linked externally has no build ID, and reports a hash of its
# own executable instead (trendvidia/go#56). Build two such tools that
# differ in content: -X empties the build ID, as gc.go's leaving it unset
# would, and -s changes the content.
env TOOLID_REWRITE=none
go build -o asm1$GOEXE -ldflags=-X=cmd/internal/objabi.buildID= cmd/asm
go build -o asm2$GOEXE '-ldflags=-X=cmd/internal/objabi.buildID= -s' cmd/asm
exec ./asm1$GOEXE -V=full
stdout '^asm1 version .* buildID=[^ /]+$'
exec ./asm2$GOEXE -V=full
stdout '^asm2 version .* buildID=[^ /]+$'

# Answering for the compiler, each gets a key of its own, the same each
# time, though both report the same version line.
env TOOLID_SUBST=$PWD/asm1$GOEXE
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
! cmp stdout base.txt
cp stdout self1.txt
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
cmp stdout self1.txt
env TOOLID_SUBST=$PWD/asm2$GOEXE
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
! cmp stdout self1.txt
env TOOLID_SUBST=

# A tool that reports no build ID at all (one that could not read its
# own executable) is keyed on its version line: it builds, gets a key of
# its own, and gets the same key each time.
env TOOLID_REWRITE=strip
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
! cmp stdout base.txt
cp stdout strip.txt
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
cmp stdout strip.txt

# The key follows that version line. Nothing else distinguishes such a
# tool, so a different one of the same version would share its key.
env TOOLID_VERSION=go1.0.2
go list -export -toolexec=$PWD/toolid -f '{{.BuildID}}' ./p
! cmp stdout strip.txt
! cmp stdout base.txt

-- go.mod --
module example.com/toolid

go 1.27
-- p/p.go --
package p

func F() int { return 1 }
-- cmd/toolid/main.go --
// Command toolid runs a tool and, when asked for -V=full, reports it as
// a release (so that cmd/go takes its release path whatever this tree's
// VERSION), $TOOLID_VERSION or go1.0.1, and rewrites its build ID as
// $TOOLID_REWRITE says, as a different compiler binary would. With
// $TOOLID_SUBST set, that binary answers -V=full in the tool's place.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

func main() {
	tool, args := os.Args[1], os.Args[2:]
	cmd := exec.Command(tool, args...)
	cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if len(args) == 0 || args[0] != "-V=full" {
		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	if subst := os.Getenv("TOOLID_SUBST"); subst != "" {
		cmd = exec.Command(subst, args...)
		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	}
	out, err := cmd.Output()
	if err != nil {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	// "compile version devel go1.N-... buildID=a/c" or
	// "compile version go1.N.M X:exp buildID=a/c".
	f := strings.Fields(string(out))
	if len(f) < 3 || f[1] != "version" {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "toolid: unexpected -V=full output %q\n", out)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	version := os.Getenv("TOOLID_VERSION")
	if version == "" {
		version = "go1.0.1"
	}
	name := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(tool), ".exe")
	line := []string{name, "version", version}
	for _, field := range f[3:] {
		if strings.HasPrefix(field, "X:") {
			line = append(line, field)
		}
	}
	if id, ok := strings.CutPrefix(f[len(f)-1], "buildID="); ok {
		switch os.Getenv("TOOLID_REWRITE") {
		case "content":
			id = id[:strings.LastIndex(id, "/")+1] + "rewrittencontentid"
		case "action":
			id = "rewrittenactionid" + id[strings.Index(id, "/"):]
		case "strip":
			id = ""
		}
		if id != "" {
			line = append(line, "buildID="+id)
		}
	}
	fmt.Println(strings.Join(line, " "))
}
